title: A Café Owner's Idea
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who owned a small café. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man was looking at the empty tables in his café.
scenes: コマ1:昼間なのにカフェの席はほとんど空いている。店主の男性が困った顔で店内を見ている。
コマ2:「That night」。男性が妻と話している。パソコンの画面に「Free Wi-Fi & Study Space」という案内を作っている。
コマ3:「A few weeks later」。カフェは学生やパソコンで仕事をする人でいっぱい。男性は笑顔でコーヒーを運んでいる。
コマ4:「A month later」。満席だが、客は飲み物1杯で何時間も座っている。入口では、家族連れが入れずに帰ろうとしており、男性が困った顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a man was looking at the empty tables in his café. Even though it was lunchtime, there were very few customers, and he looked worried. That night, he talked with his wife about how to attract more customers. He decided to offer free Wi-Fi and a study space, and he made a sign about it on his computer. A few weeks later, the café was full of students and people working on laptops, and the man was happily serving coffee. A month later, the café was still full, but the customers were sitting for hours with only one drink. The man was troubled to see that a family could not find a table and was about to leave.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm glad the café is busy, but I'm not making much money if people stay all day with one drink. Maybe I should introduce a time limit or ask customers to order something every two hours."

questions.question: Do you think small local shops can compete with large chain stores?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they can. Small shops can offer more personal service and unique products that chain stores don't have. Many customers also like supporting local businesses because they help their community.

questions.question: Should companies allow more employees to work from home?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Working from home saves time and money on commuting, and many people can concentrate better without office distractions. However, companies should still have regular meetings in person so that teams can communicate well.

title: A Recycling Project at School
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a girl who wanted to reduce waste at her school. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a girl noticed a lot of plastic bottles in the trash can at her school.
scenes: コマ1:学校のごみ箱がペットボトルであふれている。女子生徒がそれを見て驚いている。
コマ2:「The next day」。女子生徒が生徒会の会議で、リサイクル箱を設置する案を発表している。先生や生徒がうなずいている。
コマ3:「A few weeks later」。廊下に分別用の箱が並び、生徒たちがペットボトルを正しく入れている。
コマ4:「A month later」。リサイクル箱の中に、食べ残しやお菓子の袋などのごみが混ざっている。女子生徒が箱をのぞき込み、がっかりしている。
narrationSample: One day, a girl noticed a lot of plastic bottles in the trash can at her school. She was surprised that so many bottles were being thrown away. The next day, she suggested setting up recycling boxes at a student council meeting, and the teachers and students agreed with her idea. A few weeks later, recycling boxes had been placed in the hallway, and students were putting their bottles in them correctly. A month later, however, the girl looked into one of the boxes and was disappointed to see that food waste and snack bags had been mixed in with the bottles.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the girl, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "It's frustrating that people aren't separating their trash properly. I should make clearer signs and maybe explain the rules to each class."

questions.question: Do you think schools should do more to teach students about environmental problems?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. If children learn about environmental problems at school, they are more likely to develop good habits, such as recycling and saving energy. They can also share what they learn with their families.

questions.question: Should the government make companies reduce the amount of plastic packaging they use?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Plastic packaging creates a huge amount of waste, and much of it ends up in the ocean. If the government sets rules, companies will have to develop more environmentally friendly packaging.

title: A Business Trip Abroad
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who went on a business trip. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man's boss asked him to go on a business trip to Singapore.
scenes: コマ1:上司が男性に「Singapore — Meeting with Client」と書かれた書類を渡している。男性は少し緊張した表情。
コマ2:「The night before the trip」。男性が自宅でプレゼン資料を何度も練習している。スーツケースが横に置いてある。
コマ3:「At the meeting」。男性が顧客の前で発表しており、顧客たちは満足そうにうなずいている。
コマ4:「At the airport」。帰りの空港で、出発案内板に「Canceled」と表示されている。男性は困った顔で時計を見ている。
narrationSample: One day, a man's boss asked him to go on a business trip to Singapore to meet an important client. The man looked a little nervous. The night before the trip, he practiced his presentation again and again at home, with his suitcase packed next to him. At the meeting, he gave his presentation, and the clients nodded and looked very satisfied. However, at the airport on his way home, he saw that his flight had been canceled. He looked at his watch and wondered how he would get home in time.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "What bad luck! I need to contact my boss and the airline right away to find another flight. At least the meeting went well."

questions.question: Do you think online meetings will replace business trips in the future?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think they will replace many business trips, but not all of them. Online meetings save time and money, but meeting in person is still important for building trust with new clients.

questions.question: Should Japanese companies do more to train employees to work internationally?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they should. As businesses become more global, employees need language skills and an understanding of different cultures. Training programs and overseas assignments can help them work effectively with people from other countries.

title: A Volunteer at an Animal Shelter
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who volunteered at an animal shelter. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a woman saw a poster asking for volunteers at an animal shelter.
scenes: コマ1:駅の掲示板に「Volunteers Wanted — City Animal Shelter」というポスター。女性が興味深そうに見ている。
コマ2:「The following weekend」。女性が保護施設で犬の散歩をしたり、えさをあげたりしている。
コマ3:「A month later」。女性が1匹の犬と特に仲良くなり、犬が女性にしっぽを振っている。
コマ4:「The next week」。女性が施設に来ると、その犬の檻に「Adopted」という札がかかっている。女性は寂しそうに檻を見ている。
narrationSample: One day, a woman saw a poster at the station asking for volunteers at the city animal shelter. She looked interested. The following weekend, she started volunteering at the shelter, walking dogs and feeding them. A month later, she had become especially close to one dog, which always wagged its tail when it saw her. The next week, when she arrived at the shelter, she found a sign on the dog's cage that said "Adopted." She looked at the empty cage and felt a little sad.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'll miss that dog, but I'm happy that he has found a loving family. There are many other dogs here that need my help."

questions.question: Do you think more people should do volunteer work?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Volunteer work helps people in need and makes communities stronger. It also gives volunteers new experiences and a sense of purpose.

questions.question: Should people be required to get a license before owning a pet?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Some people buy pets without understanding the responsibility involved, and later they abandon them. A license system would make sure that owners know how to take care of animals properly.

title: A New Bicycle Lane
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who rode his bicycle to work. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man was riding his bicycle to work on a busy road.
scenes: コマ1:男性が交通量の多い道路を自転車で走っている。車がすぐ横を通り、男性は危なそうにしている。
コマ2:「A few days later」。男性が市役所の窓口で、自転車専用レーンの設置を求める意見書を出している。
コマ3:「Several months later」。道路に自転車専用レーンができ、男性が安全に走っている。ほかにも自転車の人が増えている。
コマ4:「The next week」。自転車レーンに配達のトラックが止まっていて、男性は車道に出なければならず、困った顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a man was riding his bicycle to work on a busy road. Cars were passing very close to him, and he felt it was dangerous. A few days later, he went to city hall and submitted a request for a bicycle lane. Several months later, a bicycle lane had been built on the road, and the man was riding safely. More people had started cycling, too. However, the next week, a delivery truck was parked in the bicycle lane, and the man had to ride onto the road. He looked annoyed.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "It's dangerous when trucks park in the bicycle lane. The city should put up signs or fine drivers who block the lane."

questions.question: Do you think more people will use bicycles to commute in the future?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. More people are becoming interested in their health and the environment, and electric bicycles make it easier to travel longer distances. If cities build more safe bike lanes, many people will choose to cycle.

questions.question: Should local governments listen more to residents' opinions when making decisions?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they should. Residents know the problems in their neighborhoods better than anyone else. If governments listen to them, they can make policies that really meet people's needs.

title: A Family Garden
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a family who wanted to grow their own vegetables. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a family was shopping for vegetables at the supermarket.
scenes: コマ1:スーパーで、母親が野菜の値札を見て驚いている。値段が高い。
コマ2:「That weekend」。家族全員で庭に野菜の苗を植えている。子どもが楽しそうに水をやっている。
コマ3:「Two months later」。庭にはトマトやきゅうりがたくさん実り、家族が収穫を喜んでいる。
コマ4:「The next morning」。庭の野菜が鳥に食べられて荒らされている。家族ががっかりして見ている。
narrationSample: One day, a family was shopping for vegetables at the supermarket, and the mother was surprised at how expensive they were. That weekend, the whole family planted vegetables in their garden, and the children happily watered the plants. Two months later, there were many tomatoes and cucumbers in the garden, and the family was pleased to harvest them. However, the next morning, they found that birds had eaten some of the vegetables and damaged the garden. Everyone was disappointed.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the mother, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "What a shame! We worked so hard on this garden. We should put a net over the vegetables to protect them from the birds."

questions.question: Do you think children should learn about growing food?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Growing food teaches children where their food comes from and helps them appreciate the work of farmers. It can also encourage them to eat more vegetables.

questions.question: Should the government do more to support farmers in Japan?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Many farmers are getting older, and few young people want to take over farms. The government should provide financial support and training so that Japan can maintain its food supply.

title: An Overseas Student
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a student who studied abroad. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a university student received a letter accepting her into a study abroad program.
scenes: コマ1:女子学生が「Study Abroad Program — Accepted」という手紙を読んで喜んでいる。
コマ2:「A few months later」。外国の教室で、女子学生が他の学生と話せず、一人で座っている。
コマ3:「Several weeks later」。女子学生が国際交流のパーティーで、いろいろな国の学生と楽しそうに話している。
コマ4:「At the end of the program」。空港で友人たちと別れを惜しみ、女子学生が涙ぐんでいる。
narrationSample: One day, a university student received a letter accepting her into a study abroad program, and she was very happy. A few months later, she was sitting alone in a classroom overseas because she found it difficult to talk with the other students. Several weeks later, however, she went to an international party, where she enjoyed talking with students from many countries. At the end of the program, she said goodbye to her friends at the airport and became tearful because she did not want to leave them.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the student, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm so sad to leave my friends, but I'm glad I came here. I'll keep in touch with them online and visit them again someday."

questions.question: Do you think more young people should study abroad?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Studying abroad helps young people improve their language skills and understand different cultures. These experiences are very useful in today's global society.

questions.question: Should universities teach more classes in English?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they should, at least in some subjects. Classes in English can attract international students and help Japanese students prepare for global careers. However, universities need enough teachers who can teach well in English.

title: A Neighborhood Festival
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who organized a neighborhood festival. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man noticed that his neighbors rarely talked to each other.
scenes: コマ1:マンションの廊下で住民同士がすれ違うが、誰もあいさつをしていない。男性がそれを見て考え込んでいる。
コマ2:「A few weeks later」。男性が近所の人たちと、夏祭りの計画を話し合っている。
コマ3:「On the day of the festival」。公園で屋台や子どもの遊びが行われ、住民たちが楽しそうに交流している。
コマ4:「The next morning」。公園にごみが散らかっていて、男性が一人で掃除をしながら疲れた顔をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a man noticed that his neighbors rarely talked to each other. People passed each other in the hallway without saying hello. A few weeks later, the man was discussing plans for a summer festival with some of his neighbors. On the day of the festival, there were food stalls and games for children in the park, and the residents were enjoying talking with each other. However, the next morning, the park was full of litter, and the man was cleaning it up by himself. He looked tired.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "The festival was a success, but I can't clean all of this by myself. Next time, I'll ask volunteers to help with cleaning up after the event."

questions.question: Do you think people today have less connection with their neighbors than in the past?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Many people are busy with work and spend their free time online. Also, people move more often than before, so it is harder to build relationships with neighbors.

questions.question: Should local governments spend more money on community events?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they should. Community events help people get to know each other, which is important for safety and for helping each other during disasters. The cost is small compared to these benefits.

title: A Health Plan
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who wanted to improve his health. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a man received the results of his health check at work.
scenes: コマ1:男性が健康診断の結果を見て驚いている。「Weight: Too high」と書いてある。
コマ2:「The next morning」。男性が早起きしてジョギングをしている。
コマ3:「Three months later」。男性がやせて、体重計を見て喜んでいる。
コマ4:「At a party」。会社のパーティーで、同僚たちがケーキや揚げ物を勧めていて、男性が断るのに困っている。
narrationSample: One day, a man received the results of his health check at work and was surprised to find that his weight was too high. The next morning, he got up early and started jogging. Three months later, he had lost weight, and he was very happy when he looked at the scale. However, at a company party, his colleagues kept offering him cake and fried food, and he did not know how to refuse.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I don't want to be rude to my colleagues, but I've worked hard to lose weight. I'll explain that I'm trying to eat healthily and just have a small piece."

questions.question: Do you think companies should be responsible for their employees' health?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, to some extent. Employees spend a lot of time at work, so companies can help by offering health checks and encouraging exercise. Healthy employees are also more productive.

questions.question: Should the government do more to encourage people to exercise?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. As the population ages, medical costs are rising. If the government builds more parks and sports facilities and runs health campaigns, more people will exercise and stay healthy.

title: A Lost Wallet
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who lost her wallet. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a woman was shopping at a busy market.
scenes: コマ1:女性が市場で買い物をしている。かばんから財布が落ちているが、本人は気づいていない。
コマ2:「A few minutes later」。レジで女性が財布がないことに気づき、慌ててかばんの中を探している。
コマ3:「That evening」。交番に男子高校生が財布を届けている。警察官が受け取っている。
コマ4:「The next day」。女性が交番で財布を受け取り、お礼の手紙を書こうとしているが、届けた人の名前がわからず困っている。
narrationSample: One day, a woman was shopping at a busy market. She did not notice that her wallet had fallen out of her bag. A few minutes later, when she went to pay, she realized that her wallet was missing and searched her bag in a panic. That evening, a high school student took the wallet to a police box, and a police officer received it. The next day, the woman got her wallet back at the police box. She wanted to write a thank-you letter, but she was troubled because she did not know the name of the person who had found it.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm so grateful to the person who returned my wallet. I'll ask the police officer if they can pass a thank-you message to the student."

questions.question: Do you think people today are less willing to help strangers?
questions.sampleAnswer: No, I don't think so. Many people still help strangers, for example by returning lost items or giving directions. In fact, social media sometimes encourages people to help others by sharing kind stories.

questions.question: Should more security cameras be installed in public places?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Security cameras can help prevent crimes and help the police find criminals. However, there should be strict rules about how the recordings are used to protect people's privacy.

title: Working at a Hotel
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman who worked at a hotel. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a woman working at a hotel front desk was having trouble communicating with a foreign guest.
scenes: コマ1:ホテルのフロントで、女性が外国人客の言葉を理解できず困っている。客も困った顔。
コマ2:「That evening」。女性が帰宅後、英会話のテキストで勉強している。
コマ3:「A few months later」。女性がフロントで外国人客と笑顔で英語で会話している。
コマ4:「The next day」。上司が女性に「Training Manager」と書かれた辞令を見せている。女性は驚いている。
narrationSample: One day, a woman working at a hotel front desk was having trouble communicating with a foreign guest. Both of them looked confused. That evening, she started studying English with a textbook after she got home. A few months later, she was talking with foreign guests in English with a smile at the front desk. The next day, her manager showed her a document saying that she had been appointed training manager, and she was very surprised.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm happy that my hard work has been recognized, but I'm a little nervous about training other staff. I'll do my best to share what I've learned."

questions.question: Do you think Japan is ready to welcome more foreign tourists?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think Japan has improved a lot, but there is still more to do. For example, more signs and information should be available in other languages, and popular tourist areas need to deal with overcrowding.

questions.question: Should companies pay for their employees to learn new skills?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they should. When employees learn new skills, such as languages, they can do their jobs better, which benefits the company. It also shows employees that the company values them.

title: A Smartphone-Free Weekend
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a family who spent too much time on their smartphones. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a father noticed that everyone in his family was looking at their smartphones during dinner.
scenes: コマ1:夕食の席で、家族全員がスマートフォンを見ていて、誰も話していない。父親が不満そうに見ている。
コマ2:「The next weekend」。父親が「No Smartphone Weekend」と書いた紙を見せ、家族のスマホを箱に入れている。子どもたちは不満そう。
コマ3:「That afternoon」。家族でボードゲームをして笑っている。
コマ4:「That evening」。父親が仕事の電話に出られなかったため、上司から大事な連絡を見逃したことに気づき、慌てている。
narrationSample: One day, a father noticed that everyone in his family was looking at their smartphones during dinner, and no one was talking. He was unhappy about this. The next weekend, he announced a "No Smartphone Weekend" and put everyone's phones into a box. The children did not look happy about it. That afternoon, however, the family played board games together and laughed a lot. That evening, the father realized that he had missed an important message from his boss because his phone had been in the box, and he panicked.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the father, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Oh no, I should have checked my phone at least once. I need to call my boss and explain. Next time, I'll make a rule that allows us to check for emergencies."

questions.question: Do you think children today spend too much time on smartphones?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Many children use their smartphones for hours every day, which can affect their sleep, eyesight, and studies. Parents should help them set limits.

questions.question: Should companies stop contacting employees outside working hours?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Employees need time to rest and spend with their families. Some countries have introduced laws that give workers the right to disconnect, and I think this is a good idea.
